clue.text: Reveal love in declaration of intent

parts.note: to manifest something is to reveal or display it
love is zero in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone discloses their feelings within a formal statement of plans.
explanation.definitionFit: A political party publishes its programme of intended policies as a public statement of aims.

clue.text: Mike, old codger, mostly makes coffee

parts.note: M is Mike in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a chap is a man or fellow, like a codger

explanation.surface: Mike, an elderly fellow, usually brews the coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a type of fine coffee, named after the Yemeni port.

clue.text: A siesta in garden apartment

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone takes an afternoon snooze in their ground-floor flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A short sleep during the day, especially after lunch, is a siesta.

clue.text: Put out food for bird

parts.note: in cricket, to field is to put out the batsman's shots, and fielders put out batsmen
fare is food or provisions

explanation.surface: Someone sets out food for a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The fieldfare is a large thrush that winters in Britain.

clue.text: Check clubs in haunts abroad

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
abroad means scattered or astray, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.definitionFit: To staunch a flow of blood is to stop or check it.

clue.text: Extra expected is late arriving

parts.note: over can mean extra or surplus, as in left over
due means expected, as in due at noon

explanation.surface: An additional train that was scheduled turns up behind time.
explanation.definitionFit: Something past the time it was due has not yet arrived and is late.

parts.note: plush means opulent or luxurious
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A traveller notes that, on top of everything, the posh hotel was not part of the package.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adverb, plus means besides or as well, an extra item being added.

clue.text: Film daughter in new local musical

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber and Rice musical

clue.text: Setter I've trained brings item used during dinner?

indicators.note: trained suggests reshaping, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The setter has been schooled in table manners at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A napkin, laid on the lap while eating; the question mark marks a description by example.

clue.text: Gear to boast about

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to brag is to boast

explanation.surface: Clothing worth showing off about.

clue.text: Bobby's first to explore thicket

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is wanted

explanation.surface: A police officer is the first to search a patch of dense woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: BOBBY is British slang for a policeman (after Sir Robert Peel); the apostrophe-S is kept, giving COPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A copse is a small group of trees and undergrowth, much the same as a thicket.

clue.text: Boy, a youth who drowned saving ten

parts.note: in Greek myth Leander drowned swimming the Hellespont to reach Hero
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A lifeguard story: a lad who drowned while rescuing ten others.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a common male first name, so any lad might bear it.

clue.text: Left behind, a group one day

parts.note: a band is a group, especially of musicians

explanation.surface: A musical group was left stranded one day on tour.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deserted or forsaken has been left behind by those who had it.

clue.text: Paint shapes up the wall, actually

indicators.note: up the wall means crazy, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone really is painting shapes on the wall.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used to mean in fact or as it turns out, like actually.

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading: lunch at one o'clock gives I.

clue.text: Vegetable from Spain that's stewed? Check

parts.note: CH is the chess notation for check

explanation.surface: A diner asks whether the vegetable from Spain has been stewed, and checks.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinach is a leafy green plant cooked and eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Astonishing bird grabbing beast's tail

indicators.note: grabbing means holding another piece inside

parts.note: the starling is a common songbird

indicators.note: tail means the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A surprising sight: a small bird catching hold of an animal's tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Something startling is surprising enough to astonish.

clue.text: Famous artist, English, not without heart

parts.note: Tracey Emin is a well-known British artist

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word not is removed

explanation.surface: A celebrated English artist who is not short of feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: Tracey Emin is a British artist, known for her unmade bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminent describes someone distinguished and well known in their field.

clue.text: Annoyed, pub worker about gibe

parts.note: an inn is a pub
a dig is a gibe or snide remark
the worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A bar employee is put out by a cutting remark.
explanation.definitionFit: Indignant means angered by something seen as unfair, so annoyed.

clue.text: A permit secured by the gymnast, perhaps

indicators.note: secured by means held inside, so one word encloses another

parts.note: to let is to permit or allow

explanation.surface: A gymnast obtains a permit for competing.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymnast is one example of a sportsperson trained in physical exercise.

clue.text: Something to eat with top boffin

parts.note: an egg is something to eat
the head is the top of something

explanation.surface: A scientist eats a meal with something on top.
explanation.walkthrough: BOFFIN is British slang for a scientist or brainy expert.
explanation.definitionFit: An intellectual or highbrow is informally called a brain, or a boffin.

clue.text: Delivery worker in the south of France going around with iron

indicators.note: going around means one word wraps the other

parts.note: the Midi is the name for the south of France
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A courier in Provence makes rounds while carrying an iron.
explanation.walkthrough: The courier picture hides the real job: 'Delivery' means childbirth.
explanation.definitionFit: She delivers babies, so 'delivery' is used in its childbirth sense.

clue.text: Fluid on items, slightly wet

indicators.note: fluid means not fixed, so the letters flow into a new order

explanation.surface: Liquid poured on objects leaves them damp.
explanation.definitionFit: To dampen something lightly is to make it slightly wet, here used as a verb.

clue.text: Spinner in charge provides talking point

parts.note: a top is a toy that spins

explanation.surface: A spin bowler who captains the side gives everyone something to discuss.
explanation.definitionFit: A subject for conversation or discussion is a theme people talk about.

clue.text: Jack of diamonds found under vehicle?

definitions.text: Jack of diamonds found under vehicle?

indicators.note: found under places the suit letter after the vehicle in a down answer

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A playing card turns up beneath a parked car.
explanation.definitionFit: The jack of diamonds is one of the fifty-two in a playing deck.

clue.text: Prevailing price to enter? Considerable, it's said

indicators.note: it's said marks a word heard rather than read

parts.note: great means large or considerable

parts.note: a peer is a nobleman

explanation.surface: A lord losing his temper is a chilling sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means uncanny, so frightening in a weird way.

clue.text: Purposefully, I approach breeding ground

parts.note: to near is to approach
a nest is where birds breed and raise young

explanation.surface: A determined person heads for a nesting site.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something seriously and with sincere intent is doing it purposefully.

clue.text: Become different once Raleigh beheaded?

parts.note: Sir Walter Raleigh, the Elizabethan explorer

explanation.walkthrough: Sir Walter Raleigh was beheaded in 1618, so the head of his first name goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To change or be modified in character is to become different.

clue.text: Bill in club brought over

parts.note: a bat is a club used in sport

clue.text: Breathe with difficulty when doctor comes round

parts.note: GP stands for general practitioner, a family doctor
as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

explanation.surface: A patient struggles for breath as the doctor visits.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking short, laboured breaths with an open mouth is to breathe with difficulty.

clue.text: Brownish-grey horse, and where it may be kept in a Bedfordshire town?

parts.note: a dun is a horse of greyish-brown colour

explanation.surface: A dun horse and the building it lives in, in an English county town.
explanation.walkthrough: Dunstable is a market town in Bedfordshire, an English county north of London.
